summary: Made parallel output order explicit, added a bounded progress-report accumulator, and measured sequential, file-order parallel and completion-order transport. The production default remains file-enumeration order; ordered SQL remains a residual semantic boundary.

review.reviewer: separate grill-code review pass (no independent subagent was available)

startingState.worktree: Tracked files were clean before W11-S05 implementation; ignored campaign state had W11-S05 active and was not included in the scope commit.
startingState.aheadNote: The ahead count includes reachable completed Search scope commits through W11-S04; no upstream changes were present.

implementation.scopeBoundary: Only the owning repository's Search production, benchmark, test and planning-documentation files changed, plus this scope's campaign evidence. No sibling repository, package version, publication state or native backend was changed.
implementation.orderingContract: The coordinator exposes file-enumeration order and completion order as explicit transport modes. Search keeps bounded file-enumeration order as its production default; completion order is a multiset-preserving internal candidate and is not an SQL ORDER BY guarantee.
implementation.progressContract: Per-file emitted-row counts are accumulated and reported at a configured positive interval, with a final successful flush. Zero-row files do not invoke the progress callback.
implementation.lifecycleContract: The existing bounded worker/channel lifecycle is retained. Completion waits remain cancellation-aware, successful work completes its output and completion signal, and failure cleanup disposes queued and active work.
implementation.measurement: Added measure-parallel-cost with a deterministic 48-file by 128-row workload, one excluded warmup and seven randomized paired trials. It compares output counts and hashes, sorted result hashes, timing, sorting timing, coordinator-thread allocations and progress callback counts, plus a 256-file no-match workload.
implementation.dependencyNote: The benchmark project now references Musoq.Schema directly because the Search project intentionally excludes runtime assets and the standalone benchmark must resolve its coordinator contracts when run with --no-build.

scenarios: Existing worker-bound, cancellation, first-failure and repeated-cleanup coordinator tests.
Completion-order output preserves the sequential row multiset.
Progress aggregation reports bounded positive batches and ignores no-match files.
Compiled ordered queries remain deterministic across repeated parallel runs.
Existing slice, residual predicate, join and tie-order semantics remain green.

parallelCostMeasurement.workload: 48 files x 128 rows; deterministic bounded spin-wait and one owned row chunk per file

commands.argv: git diff --cached --check; JSON parse validation; source manifest and artifact hash validation; campaign validator

gateResults.evidence: The exact Release owning-repository suite completed across 21 projects with 1,560 total tests, 1,526 passed, 0 failed and 34 classified skips; the Search suite and W11 focused suite also passed.

The separate review approved explicit transport ordering, bounded progress accounting, lifecycle preservation and the measurement limitations; the exact scope and repository trailers are required for completion.
Sequential, file-order parallel and completion-order workloads emitted equal row counts and equal sorted multiset hashes; repeated compiled ordered queries remained deterministic.

The coordinator retains bounded workers, in-flight files and per-file channels; progress is interval-bounded, no-match scans report zero rows, cancellation-aware waits remain in place, and cleanup tests pass.

knownLimitations: The benchmark uses a deterministic in-memory coordinator workload; it is not a native backend or a full filesystem-to-query end-to-end measurement.
The reported timing is an observation on this host. It measures coordinator-thread allocations, not total process allocation, and makes no universal throughput claim.
Completion order is an explicit internal candidate only; the production Search default remains file-enumeration order, and SQL ORDER BY retains its residual sorting cost.
The final run executed on an x64 host; ARM64 was not emulated or directly measured.
The repository suite retained 34 existing classified skips: 31 expected and 3 platform-conditional symlink skips.
A standalone benchmark dependency reference was added for Musoq.Schema; no package was published, pushed, released or installed.
